subject: Request: Lunaris fast-fallback path prioritization for pilot
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Lunaris pilot — ask to prioritize fast-fallback behavior before signature

Team — quick context: Lunaris Systems (edge compute customer) is in lock-step to sign next-week if we can guarantee a deterministic fallback to a smaller quantized variant when their avg latency for long prompts exceeds 350ms. Procurement is holding the SOW pending this commitment.

Customer ask (explicit):
- When their model request path experiences queueing or memory pressure, automatically route to a pre-approved quantized model (q4_8 variant) with consistent tokenization so outputs remain compatible.
- The fallback must be configurable per-tenant and pinned in the console (no auto-version drift).
- Provide an SLA addendum clause committing to a max failover latency of 150ms additional on fallback.

Why this matters: Lunaris is committing to a 4-region pilot (reserved capacity) and a 36-month expansion forecast; they put the fallback in the contract as a gating item. This is a $850k ARR anchor if we can deliver a clear technical approach + timeline.

Attachments: Lunaris_SOW_draft_v3.pdf, Lunaris_MVP_Roadmap.xlsx (high-level). Also shared a proposed SLA_Addendum.pdf.

Ask: Can product/engineering confirm feasibility and a scoped plan (delta work + risks) by EOW? If we can commit to a spike this week and a production shim in <= 4 weeks, I can get procurement to unblock.

Thanks —
Ben
Ben Carter | Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Lunaris pilot — ask to prioritize fast-fallback behavior before signature

Ben — thanks for the heads-up and the materials. High-level reactions:
- Product is aligned on tenant-configurable fallback rules, but we need to scope the compatibility guarantee (tokenization & deterministic outputs) carefully.
- Two questions for engineering: can we guarantee identical token boundaries between the main and quantized variant without re-tokenizing on the fly?

I propose a scoped plan:
1) Spike (3 work-days): prototype a config-driven routing shim that can swap model endpoints mid-request for tail latency events and validate tokenization parity on representative prompts.
2) Risk assessment + ops design (2 days): define monitoring hooks, rollout gating, and console UX for pinning fallback variants.
3) Production shim + canary (2-3 weeks): a minimal runtime change with a fallback registry and telemetry.

If engineering confirms the spike timeline, I can commit product resources to shepherd console flags and the policy semantics. Please confirm by EOD so Ben can push on procurement.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Senior PM, Serving & Runtime

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 09:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Lunaris pilot — ask to prioritize fast-fallback behavior before signature

Karthik / Ben — quick technical notes after an initial sync with infra:
- Feasibility: yes, we can implement a routing shim that performs a per-request decision to invoke a smaller quantized variant. The tricky part is preserving "output compatibility" — we can ensure tokenization parity by enforcing the same tokenizer and vocabulary across variants, but generation divergences remain (sampling/beam differences). We should be explicit with Lunaris about what "compatible" means (semantic parity vs byte-for-byte).
- Memory & latency: the fallback path will reduce memory pressure but may add ~80-180ms to the specific request depending on whether we warm KV cache for the quantized model. We can optimize with warmup/seeding strategies for known tenants.
- Implementation approach:
  a) routing shim + fallback registry (runtime change, ~8 engineering days full-time)
  b) console flags & per-tenant policy UI (product + frontend, ~5 days)
  c) telemetry + SLA hooks (observability + infra, ~4 days)

Total estimated effort: ~3-4 sprints if done with existing sprint capacity; if we scope to a narrow canary (Lunaris only, limited prompt shapes), we can push to a 3-week delivery with a focused bugfix cadence.

We also need legal/exec approval to include any SLA addendum language that guarantees fallback latency. Technically we can provide a target, but "contractual guarantee" is a business decision.

I'll start the spike Thursday if you mark this as priority; please confirm scope and whether Lunaris accepts a narrow canary (tenant-only, non-global) for the initial delivery.

—Dev
Dev Patel | Engineering Lead, Inference Runtime

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Elaine Park <elaine.park@lunaris.ai>, procurements@lunaris.ai
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Lunaris pilot — ask to prioritize fast-fallback behavior before signature

Thanks — that sounds reasonable. Elaine (Lunaris) confirmed that semantic parity is acceptable for the pilot; they only need to ensure downstream components behave the same (no breaking token boundary changes). They are OK with a tenant-only canary for the 1st month.

Procurement is asking for a timeline to include in the SOW: can we commit to starting the spike by Thu 9/17 and provide a demo of the spike results by 9/24? If engineering can provide the 3-week production shim timeline we can tie the SOW milestone to that delivery and sign conditional on canary success.

Deal economics: Lunaris intends to sign a reserved capacity deal for 4 regions, initial committed ARR $850k (negotiable), plus an option to expand in 2027. I can escalate an ACV-based prioritization request to Sales leadership if that helps.

Ben
Ben Carter | Enterprise AE

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Lunaris pilot — ask to prioritize fast-fallback behavior before signature

Received and documented. Executive summary for leadership:
- Action: approve a scoped Lunaris-only canary spike starting 2026-09-17; aim to demo spike results by 2026-09-24.
- Scope & risks: runtime routing shim + fallback registry (engineering spike) + console pin UX (product). Estimated minimal production delivery in 3 weeks for a tenant-scoped canary; full platform hardening will require additional sprints. Tokenization parity will be enforced; semantic differences documented in the SOW addendum.
- Contract note: legal must redact absolute SLA guarantees; instead we'll offer a target with remediation terms.

Next steps:
1) Dev to kick off the spike Thursday (standups flagged).
2) Karthik to prepare a short demo plan & success criteria.
3) Ben to push procurement the conditional-SOW language and attach the HubSpot record (HS-987654321).

Marking this as a priority and copying the relevant delivery tracks into the roadmap board.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Head of Sales Operations
